newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati asked to withdraw lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati asked to withdraw lawsuit.

text.p: The leader of Indonesia's largest Moslem organisation, known to be a supporter of ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri, on Thursday called on her to withdraw a lawsuit against the government.

Abdurrahman Wahid, leader of the 30-million strong Nahdhatul Ulama, appealed to Megawati to withdraw the suit against Armed Forces Chief General Feisal Tanjung, Interior Minster Yogie Memet and National Police Chief Lieutenant-General Dibyo Widodo.
"I appeal to Megawati to withdraw her suit (against the three) as this will not benefit her as the leader of the PDI," Wahid told reporters at the Jakarta headquarters of his group.
"What has been done by Megawati's team up to now is heading in the direction of a confrontation which is not needed."

Megawati filed the lawsuit, which also targets rivals in the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), after she was ousted by a rival faction headed by parliamentary speaker Surjadi at a government-funded congress in June.
Her civil suit seeks to declare the government's support for the congress illegal. She is seeking 51 trillion rupiah ($22 billion) in damages and her reinstatement as party leader.
The case was adjourned in the Central Jakarta State Court last week until October 10, when the panel of judges is expected to rule on whether they have the authority to hear the case.

Wahid, a liberal and outspoken figure and long-time friend of Megawati, has made a point of appearing by Megawati's side in public in recent months despite her unpopularity with the government, which no longer recognises her as PDI leader.
"I still acknowledge and support the leadership of Megawati. I will be consistent," he said.
In addition to the case against the government, military and party rivals, Megawati's legal team on Tuesday filed a suit against the East Jakarta Mayor for sealing their temporary office last week.
Megawati's supporters were expelled from PDI headquarters in central Jakarta on July 27, sparking the worst riots in the capital in more than 20 years. At least five people died.
They are also threatening to sue the General Election Institute (LPU) for refusing to accept a list of Megawati's candidates for next year's general election.
Neither Megawati nor her chief legal representative R.O. Tambunan were immediately available for comment on Wahid's appeal.
